summary: Buyant-Ukhaa International Airport (ULN) was Mongolia's primary international gateway for decades before the opening of Chinggis Khaan International Airport in 2021. Located about 18 km southwest of central Ulaanbaatar, it now primarily handles domestic flights and some international charters. The airport features a single runway and a compact terminal, offering a convenient alternative for travelers heading to the capital.
faqs:
Q: Is Buyant-Ukhaa International Airport still the main airport for Ulaanbaatar?
A: No, since July 2021, most international flights moved to the new Chinggis Khaan International Airport (UBN). Buyant-Ukhaa now mainly serves domestic flights and some international charter services.

Q: How far is Buyant-Ukhaa Airport from downtown Ulaanbaatar?
A: It is approximately 18 kilometers (11 miles) southwest of the city center, typically a 30-45 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: What airlines operate at Buyant-Ukhaa?
A: Domestic carriers like Aero Mongolia and Hunnu Air operate here, along with some international charter flights. Major international airlines have relocated to UBN.

Q: Are there public transportation options to the airport?
A: Yes, buses and taxis are available, but taxis are more common. There is no direct rail link; the airport is accessible by road.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most convenient option, with fixed rates to the city center; agree on the fare beforehand or use a ride-hailing app. Public buses (e.g., route 7) also connect the airport to Ulaanbaatar, but they can be crowded and slow. Allow extra time during rush hour, as traffic on the main road into the city can be heavy.
local_tip: If you're flying domestically, arrive early as check-in and security can be slow during peak morning departures; the terminal is small and gets crowded. Also, keep small change for luggage carts, which require a deposit.
